title: MZ Cannot read property '0' of undefined

posts.author: ZoeMoonStar
posts.body: My game was able to run the battles fine and then it just randomly stopped. I got this error in the Index, Can anyone help me?

posts.author: Canned_Dinosaur
posts.body:
ZoeMoonStar said:
My game was able to run the battles fine and then it just randomly stopped. I got this error in the Index, Can anyone help me?
Click to expand...
Doesn't make sense since in your Plugin Manager you have SVActorPositionMZ set to off yet the error occurs at that plugin. Restart RPG Maker and try again with the plugin turned off. Does the problem still occur?
Note that Battle Core already includes functionality so you should use that instead. Multiple plugins tweaking the same thing is (generally speaking) asking for conflicts.

posts.author: TheAM-Dol
posts.body:
Are you starting a new game or are you loading an old save?
Especially when changing plugins, you should always start a new save because in a way, the plugin's function gets baked into your save upon creation of the save. If you suddenly remove (or add) a plugin, that plugin's functions will go wonky or not run properly - or at all.

posts.author: caethyril
posts.body:
Note that you need to save your project to apply Plugin Manager changes, then re-launch the playtest/battle test. If you don't save, then the previous plugin settings still apply.
Edit: also, that index file is referencing MV core scripts. That might be a problem unless you're in the middle of porting this project from MV to MZ.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
additionally you should keep in mind that any error "of undefined" means that the engine has been given a reference to a data object that does not exist.
And there are very few ways that could happen:
1) loading an incompatible older savefile (for example after changes in the plugin manager you need to start new games)
2) wrong order of plugins
3) wrong or missing configuration for a plugin (there are plugins that never work as-is, they need to be configured for any specific game to work)
4) deleting database entries after they have been used in the game (the classic most often one is deleting the classes while keeping actors that use said classes)
